zh: 轮廓里的正方形总可以竖直往下挪到贴地而不越界，所以只需考虑底边贴地的正方形。边长 s 能放下，当且仅当存在一段长度至少为 s 的连续楼房，每栋都至少高 s；一段楼房 [l,r] 能放下的最大边长是 min(宽度, 段内最低高度)。
在最优段里取最矮的那栋楼 i，把段向两边扩展到第一栋比它更矮的楼为止：宽度只会变大，最低高度不变。所以只需对每栋楼考虑“以它为最低楼的极大段”，候选边长是 min(h[i], 该段宽度)。
用单调栈分别求出每栋楼左边和右边第一栋严格更矮的楼的位置 left[i]、right[i]，极大段宽度为 right[i]−left[i]−1，取所有 min(h[i], 宽度) 的最大值再平方。边长可达 3×10^6，面积约 9×10^12，要用 64 位整数；n 达三百万，要用快速读入。
en: A square inside the outline can always be moved straight down until it rests on the ground without leaving the outline, so only squares with their bottom edge on the ground matter. Side s fits if and only if some run of at least s consecutive buildings has every height at least s; a run [l,r] fits a square of side at most min(width, lowest height in the run).

In an optimal run, take its lowest building i and extend the run on both sides up to the first strictly lower building: the width can only grow and the lowest height stays the same. So it is enough to consider, for each building, the maximal run in which it is the lowest, with candidate side min(h[i], width of that run).

Use a monotonic stack to find, for each building, the positions left[i] and right[i] of the first strictly lower building on each side; the maximal run has width right[i]−left[i]−1. Take the maximum of min(h[i], width) over all buildings and square it. The side can reach 3×10^6 and the area about 9×10^12, so use 64-bit integers; n reaches three million, so use fast input.

explanationEn:
## Problem

n buildings of width 1 stand side by side in a row; building i has height cityLine[i], and their outline forms a histogram. Find the area of the largest square that fits completely inside this outline.

## Derivation

A square inside the outline can be moved straight down to the ground without crossing the boundary, so only squares whose bottom edge rests on the ground, with sides parallel to the axes, need to be considered. A square of side s fits if and only if there is a run of consecutive buildings of width ≥s in which every height is ≥s. For a run of consecutive buildings [l,r], the largest side that fits is min(r−l+1, min h[l..r]). Since widths and heights are integers, the optimal side is an integer, and the answer is the side squared.

## Algorithm

In an optimal run, take the building i of lowest height. Extending the run with i as its lowest building on both sides up to the first building shorter than it only increases the width while keeping the minimum height, so for each i it is enough to consider "the maximal run with h[i] as its minimum height", with candidate side min(h[i], width of that run). Use a monotonic stack to find, for each building, the positions of the first shorter building on its left and on its right; the answer is the maximum over all candidates, squared.

## Correctness

For any run that fits a side s, the maximal run of its lowest building i contains it, so h[i]≥s and the width of the maximal run is ≥s, giving a candidate ≥s. Conversely, every candidate corresponds to a square that really fits. So the largest candidate is the largest side.

## Numeric range

The side can reach min(n,10^8)=3×10^6, so the area is about 9×10^12; use 64-bit integers.

## Complexity

In the monotonic stack, each index is pushed and popped once: O(n) time and O(n) space.

## Independent verification

The oracle binary searches on the side: side s is feasible if and only if there is a run of length ≥s with every height ≥s, decided by a linear scan without a monotonic stack; for small domains it also enumerates every run and takes min(width, minimum height). All inputs with n=1..6 and heights 1..4 are enumerated, and the reference program is actually run on each. The formal cases cover the original examples, all heights at the maximum, all heights 1, increasing/decreasing staircases, a single tall tower, random large values and more. Four wrong programs that exit normally (a 32-bit area, computing the largest rectangle, ignoring the run width, printing the side) are each judged wrong on the formal cases.
